record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does every orientably regular d-polytope, for d ≥ 2, admit a chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 27 Does every orientably regular d-polytope admit a chiral extension (d ≥ 2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract d-polytope is a ranked partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) have ranks in {-1, 0, 1, ..., d}, with a unique minimum face of rank -1 and a unique maximum face of rank d, satisfying the diamond condition (every flag, i.e. every maximal chain, can be uniquely modified at any intermediate rank) and a strong connectivity condition on flags. Two flags are called j-adjacent if they differ exactly in their rank-j face. The automorphism group of an abstract polytope acts on flags, and the polytope is called regular if this action is transitive on flags. A regular d-polytope is called orientably regular if its automorphism group has a subgroup of index 2 that acts transitively on the "even" flags (equivalently, the flag graph admits a proper 2-coloring preserved by an index-2 subgroup of the automorphism group). A d-polytope is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits. A chiral (d+1)-polytope P is said to be a chiral extension of a d-polytope K if all facets of P are isomorphic to K.

Question: For every integer d ≥ 2, does every orientably regular d-polytope K admit a chiral extension; that is, does there exist a chiral (d+1)-polytope whose facets are all isomorphic to K?
artifact.status_search_result: Cunningham and Pellicer (Discrete Math. 2014) proved that every finite chiral d-polytope with regular facets admits a finite chiral extension, and later constructions by Montero (2020/2021) give chiral extensions with controlled Schläfli symbols under additional hypotheses. However, the general question of whether every orientably regular d-polytope (d ≥ 2) admits a chiral extension does not appear to be resolved in the literature, and recent works continue to address only special cases (e.g., toroids, polytopes with regular facets).

status_evidence.title: Chiral extensions of chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a chiral (d+1)-polytope with facets isomorphic to a given chiral d-polytope with regular facets; finite whenever the input is finite.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes chiral extensions exist for chiral polytopes with regular facets, but does not settle the orientably regular case in general.

status_evidence.title: On the Schläfli symbol of chiral extensions of polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces constructions of chiral extensions of chiral polytopes with regular facets satisfying certain conditions, with arbitrarily large last Schläfli entry.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses controlled chiral extensions, not the universal existence question for orientably regular polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Extensions of Regular Toroids
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work constructing chiral extensions for specific families (regular toroids).
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the problem is still being approached case-by-case rather than fully resolved.
